questions.text: What exact test-shell command syntax and framing should be used over UART?
questions.default: Provide a simple line-oriented ASCII shell that reads and writes the documented 32-bit register offsets.
questions.reason: The request specifies shell capabilities and baud rate, but not command syntax, framing, or response format; a line shell is easy to use from scripts.
questions.answer: Provide a simple line-oriented ASCII shell that reads and writes the documented 32-bit register offsets.

questions.text: What should happen if more than one button is pressed at the same time?
questions.default: Centre clear takes priority; otherwise up and down pressed together cancel, while their individual press counters each increment.
questions.reason: The request defines each button's individual effect but does not define priority or interaction for simultaneous presses.
questions.answer: A simultaneous clear press takes priority; otherwise up takes priority over down, so up and down do not cancel. Only the highest-priority press acts.
questions.evidence: - If several presses land on the same clock, only the highest priority acts - clear, then up, then down.

questions.text: What exact reset values and register offsets should the shell expose?
questions.default: Use the register map in this specification, with zeroed counters/control and full brightness after reset.
questions.reason: Only the desired readable and writable quantities and the design ID are specified; no address map or startup brightness is given.
questions.answer: The shell window uses absolute address `0x80 + offset`. The register map is: `0x00 COUNT` reset `0x0000`; `0x01 DUTY` reset `0x40`; `0x02 CTRL` reset `0x2`; `0x03 INPUTS` reset `null`; `0x04 PRESSES` reset `0`. Thus CTRL is not zero and DUTY is not full brightness after reset.

questions.text: What debounce duration should be used for the mechanical buttons?
questions.reason: The request requires bounce rejection but gives no interval; 10 ms is a practical mechanical-button debounce interval.

questions.text: What PWM frequency and brightness transfer curve are desired?
questions.default: Use a 256-cycle period with linear 8-bit duty control at approximately 3906 Hz.
questions.reason: The request says PWM should not flicker but does not specify frequency or transfer curve; this frequency is above visible flicker for a directly driven LED.
questions.answer: Use a 256-cycle period with linear 8-bit duty control at approximately 3906 Hz.

questions.text: What digit refresh rate should the multiplexed display use?
questions.default: Use 100000 cycles per digit slot, approximately 125 Hz across eight digits.
questions.reason: The request does not specify refresh timing; this full-frame rate is suitable to avoid visible display flicker.
questions.answer: Use 2^17 = 131,072 clocks per digit slot. The full eight-digit display refreshes at about 95 Hz, rather than 125 Hz.
questions.evidence: REFRESH_BITS: 17             # each display digit is lit for 2^17 clocks = 1.31 ms; 8 digits = 10.5 ms (95 Hz)

questions.text: Should switch brightness selection use all eight right-hand switches and what is its control-bit polarity?
questions.default: Use SW0 through SW7 when CONTROL bit 0 is one.
questions.reason: The request says eight right-hand switches and a control bit but does not identify the switch indices or selection polarity.
questions.answer: Use SW[7:0] when CTRL.DUTY_SRC is 1; the specification does not identify these switches as the “right-hand” switches.
questions.evidence: - DUTY_EFF = SW[7:0] (synchronised) if CTRL.DUTY_SRC = 1, else the DUTY register.

questions.text: How should brightness and counter digits be ordered on the physical seven-segment display?
questions.default: Show brightness on AN7:AN6, blank AN5:AN4, and show the counter on AN3:AN0 with the least-significant counter digit at AN0.
questions.reason: The request identifies left, middle, and right digit groups but does not state digit order or physical digit-enable mapping.
questions.answer: Show brightness on AN7:AN6, blank AN5:AN4, and show the counter on AN3:AN0 with the least-significant counter digit at AN0.

questions.text: Should zero brightness blank the LEDs and should maximum brightness be exactly full-on?
questions.default: Map 0 to off and 255 to continuously on.
questions.reason: The request does not specify endpoint behavior; exact endpoints are intuitive for an 8-bit brightness setting.
questions.answer: Zero brightness blanks the LEDs, but maximum brightness is not continuously on: at 255, they are on 255/256 of the time.
questions.evidence: - DUTY_EFF = 0 is fully off; 255 is on 255/256 of the time. Brightness is linear in DUTY_EFF (no gamma).

questions.text: What should happen to button press counters when the centre button clears the main counter?
questions.default: Only the main 16-bit counter is cleared; event counters continue accumulating until CPU reset.
questions.reason: The request says centre clears 'it' (the counter) and separately asks for press counts, without requesting a way to clear those counts.
questions.answer: Only the main 16-bit counter is cleared; event counters continue accumulating until CPU reset.

questions.text: What serial framing and exact baud divider should be used?
questions.default: Use 8N1 and a divider of 868 clk100mhz cycles per bit.
questions.reason: Only nominal 115200 baud is specified; 8N1 is conventional and the integer divider gives a close baud rate from 100 MHz.
questions.answer: Use 8N1 and a divider of 868 clk100mhz cycles per bit.
